newsitem.title: USA: Pamela Lee breach of contract trial ends.
newsitem.headline: Pamela Lee breach of contract trial ends.

text.p: A film company suing actress Pamela Anderson Lee for backing out of a movie deal said on Monday she never objected to sex scenes when she first read the script and gave no hint she would withdraw from the project.
But the lawyer for the former "Baywatch" TV star told the court there was no binding agreement and that Lee had the right of any woman to decide what to do with her own body.
"We didn't have mutual assent. They (film producers) didn't have a memo, didn't have a signed napkin," Lee's attorney Major Langer said in his closing argument.
"Pamela Anderson Lee was going to do what she wanted with her body and she didn't want to do simulated sex," he said.
After the defence wound up its argument, Judge David Horowitz adjourned the non-jury trial, saying he would issue his verdict sometime next week.

Lee was sued for $5 million by The Private Movie Co., which alleges she broke a deal to star in "Hello, She Lied" for up to $200,000 because she was offered $500,000 to make the feature film "Barb Wire," which turned out to be a box-office flop.
The Canadian-born actress, who is married to rock drummer Tommy Lee of the band Motley Crue, claimed she changed her mind about making "Hello, She Lied" after seeing the script.
